2.4 Overall Eﬃciency
We have examined both the algorithmic and computational eﬃciency of MCMC algorithms, each
of which fundamentally aﬀect overall MCMC eﬃciency. We deﬁne the overall eﬃciency of Ψ simply
as E(Ψ) = A(Ψ)/C(Ψ). We consider this to be a sensible measure of the overall eﬃciency of an
MCMC algorithm, since E(Ψ) may be interpreted as the number of eﬀective samples produced per
unit of MCMC algorithm runtime, for the slowest mixing model parameter. If we can construct Ψ
to maximize E(Ψ), then Ψ is the most time-eﬃcient MCMC algorithm for generating eﬀectively
independent samples to approximate the true, joint posterior distribution of Θ.
That being said, from our examination of algorithmic and computational eﬃciency, it is not
immediately clear how to balance tradeoﬀs between A(Ψ) and C(Ψ) to maximize E(Ψ). We have
generally considered the two boundary-case algorithms Ψ scalar and Ψ block, but a huge number of
intermediate algorithms exist. For Ψ ∈ ΨM, we may gain useful insights regarding the factors
aﬀecting E(Ψ) in terms of the properties of each ψi. C(Ψ) = ∑k
i=1 C(ψi), and the values A(Ψ, θi)
